history.title: Warehouse Robot Saturation Bottleneck

style_when: scale is the story — a port, a refinery, a data centre hall, a rail yard, a skyline of cranes — and the reader needs to feel how big it is
prompt: Telephoto compression, 200mm long-lens view of industrial infrastructure. A dense, deep line of identical low-profile warehouse transport robots queued motionless along a polished concrete logistics floor, bottlenecked under high-contrast industrial directional lighting. Stacked overlapping layers of automated machinery stretching into the distance with crystal-clear telephoto distance clarity. Deep shadows, crisp atmospheric depth, no people in the foreground, cool teal and amber palette, editorial cover standard.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random letters, numbers, UI, watermarks, typography, labels
rationale: A long-lens compressed view emphasizes the scale and the physical queuing of identical machines, perfectly illustrating the concept of 'capital standing still' when too many robots are deployed.
cue: every robot past saturation is capex
subject: a dense queue of automated warehouse robots bottlenecked in a logistics facility
core_thesis: A fixed robot-to-station ratio fails as catalogue size grows, leading to idle machines and wasted capital once human picker saturation is reached.
core_conflict: Capital expenditure on additional robots vs. the fixed throughput limit of human pickers.
composition: off-centre telephoto compression with deep layering
